items.number: Vet Clin North Am Small Anim Pract 2026
items.title: Computer vision and deep learning in small animal cytology and slide review
items.journal: Veterinary Clinics of North America: Small Animal Practice, 2026
items.summary: An invited review of computer vision fundamentals for veterinary cytology, current scientific progress, and publication guidelines. Examines how nine veterinary organizations address AI in their position or policy statements, alongside industrial implementation and the case for AI literacy in continuing education.

thumb.alt: Four computer-vision tasks compared: image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation and instance segmentation on cytology cells

items.title: Applying artificial intelligence to automate clinical data extraction from veterinary electronic health records: a practical guidance and comparative scoping review
items.journal: Veterinary Pathology, 2026 · special issue on artificial intelligence
items.summary: Screened 5,796 papers and included 54 studies (23 veterinary, 31 human) on AI-based clinical data extraction. Provides a step-by-step framework for data preparation, platform and privacy decisions, and prompt engineering, with a worked case study extracting 62 variables from canine pancreatitis records.

thumb.alt: Framework figure: planning, refinement and testing phases of LLM-based clinical data extraction, with a canine pancreatitis use case

items.title: Curriculum framework for artificial intelligence literacy in veterinary education
items.summary: A five-module framework for teaching AI literacy in veterinary curricula, with an implementation case study of VTPB 948 at Texas A&M University.

thumb.alt: Illustration of five stacked numbered bars representing the five-module AI literacy curriculum

items.title: Renal single-Cell RNA sequencing and digital cytometry in dogs with X-linked hereditary nephropathy
items.authors: Candice P. Chu, Daniel Osorio, and Mary B. Nabity
items.summary: Applied single-cell RNA sequencing to profile renal cortical tissues from dogs with X-linked hereditary nephropathy. Recovered over 13,000 cells and identified 11 cell types. Digital cytometry confirmed disease-related shifts in renal cell composition across CKD progression.

items.title: Urinary microRNA as biomarkers for chronic kidney disease in dogs and cats: updates and challenges
items.authors: Candice P. Chu, and Mary B. Nabity
items.summary: Comprehensive review of urinary miRNAs as non-invasive biomarkers for CKD in companion animals. Addresses preanalytical factors, RNA isolation methods, sequencing analysis, and normalization strategies.

items.title: ChatGPT in veterinary medicine: a practical guidance of generative artificial intelligence in clinics, education, and research
items.summary: Practical synthesis of ChatGPT applications in veterinary clinical, educational, and research domains. Actionable guidance for professionals without a programming background.

_thumbNote: All publication thumbnails live in assets/thumbs/ capped at 420px wide — they render into a 140px slot, so nothing larger is worth shipping. Entries whose article has no reusable figure (or where reproducing a publisher figure would raise licensing questions) use a generated illustration in the site palette; their alt text must describe them as illustrations, never as figures from the paper.
